note: Editorial reconstruction of training links (PhD, postdoc). Each published link is backed by a PubMed co-authorship at the mentor's institution and an independent page naming the mentor.

edges.work: Developed isotope-coded affinity tags (ICAT) for quantitative proteomics.
Showed that mTORC2, not mTORC1, phosphorylates SGK1, set NDRG1 phosphorylation as an mTORC2 readout, and characterized the mTOR inhibitor Ku-0063794.
edges.focus: Cancer-signalling drug discovery in industry, building on mTORC2/SGK1 and PI3K-mTOR inhibitor pharmacology.
edges.focus_beginner: He found which mTOR machine switches on a kinase called SGK1 and helped test early drugs that block mTOR directly.

edges.work: Showed that TFEB links autophagy to lysosome production and is controlled by nutrient-dependent phosphorylation (ERK2, mTORC1) (Science 2011).
edges.own_lab: Settembre Lab, Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine (TIGEM) (Pozzuoli, Naples, Italy)
edges.focus: Selective autophagy (ER-phagy) and lysosome biogenesis in physiology and lysosomal storage disorders.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how cells clear out damaged parts and junk, and how to fix this cleaning in rare genetic diseases.

edges.period: 2004-2006, then senior research associate to 2011 (ETH Zurich)
edges.work: Solved crystal structures of fungal and mammalian fatty acid synthase.
Showed that Ames dwarf mice, lacking growth hormone, prolactin and TSH, live much longer than normal siblings (Nature 1996).
edges.own_lab: Brown-Borg Lab, University of North Dakota School of Medicine & Health Sciences (Grand Forks, North Dakota, USA)
edges.focus: Growth hormone signalling, methionine metabolism and stress resistance in long-lived mouse models.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies why mice with low growth hormone live much longer, and what that says about ageing.

edges.work: Studied how mTORC1 and ERK signalling control purine and nucleotide synthesis, including ERK2 phosphorylation of PFAS, and purine metabolism in glioblastoma drug resistance.
edges.own_lab: EAL-METABO Lab, Dept. of Toxicology and Cancer Biology, University of Kentucky (Lexington, Kentucky, USA)
edges.focus: Cancer metabolism, with emphasis on signalling control of nucleotide metabolism, neuroimmunometabolism and obesity.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how cancer cells rewire their chemistry to make DNA building blocks fast, and how to block that.

edges.work: Showed in flies that lowering TOR activity extends lifespan in a diet-dependent way, linking TOR to dietary restriction (Curr Biol 2004).
edges.own_lab: Kapahi Lab, Buck Institute for Research on Aging (Novato, California, USA)
edges.focus: Nutrient signalling, dietary restriction, glycation and metabolism in aging and age-related disease, in worms, flies and mice.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how what and how much we eat changes the speed of aging, using worms, flies and mice.

edges.work: Showed that RSK1 phosphorylates TSC2 at Ser1798 downstream of Ras/MAPK, linking MAPK signalling to mTORC1 (PNAS 2004).
edges.own_lab: Roux Lab, IRIC, Universite de Montreal (Montreal, Quebec, Canada)
edges.focus: Ras/MAPK-RSK signalling, crosstalk with mTORC1, and translational control in cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how a second growth-signal pathway (Ras-MAPK) plugs into mTOR and the protein-making machinery.

edges.work: Showed that TSC1-TSC2 inhibits mTOR signalling and acts as a GAP for Rheb, placing Rheb between TSC and mTOR.
edges.own_lab: Tee Lab, Division of Cancer & Genetics, Cardiff University (Cardiff, Wales, UK)
edges.focus: mTOR signalling in inherited tumour syndromes (TSC, Birt-Hogg-Dube, NF1) and its effects on autophagy, energy metabolism, angiogenesis and inflammation.
edges.focus_beginner: He uses rare genetic diseases where mTOR is stuck 'on' to learn how mTOR drives tumours and to find drugs for them.

edges.work: Solved structures of NPC1 domains bound to NPC2, explaining how cholesterol leaves lysosomes.

edges.period: about 2001-2005 (MRC Dunn Human Nutrition Unit, Cambridge)
edges.work: Measured where mitochondria make superoxide and showed that mild uncoupling strongly lowers it.
Showed that blocking the Asp664 caspase site of APP prevents Alzheimer-like pathology in transgenic mice (PNAS 2006).
Identified TSC2 as a direct Akt substrate and helped establish Rheb as the GTPase target of the TSC complex upstream of mTOR.
edges.own_lab: Manning Lab, Dept. of Molecular Metabolism, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: How the PI3K-Akt-TSC-mTORC1 network controls nucleotide, lipid and protein synthesis in physiology, cancer, metabolic and neurological disease, and aging.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how insulin and growth signals flip the mTOR switch and how that changes what a cell builds and burns.

edges.work: Showed that LKB1 is needed for AMPK activity in the liver, controls glucose levels through CRTC2, and is required for metformin's glucose-lowering effect (Science 2005).
edges.own_lab: Shaw Lab, Molecular and Cell Biology Laboratory, Salk Institute for Biological Studies (La Jolla, California, USA)
edges.focus: The LKB1-AMPK energy-sensing pathway, its control of mTORC1, autophagy and mitophagy (ULK1), metabolism, and LKB1-mutant lung cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies the cell's fuel gauge (LKB1-AMPK), which brakes growth when energy runs low and is broken in some lung cancers.

edges.work: Purified and characterised PDK1, the kinase that phosphorylates Akt/PKB at Thr308.
Used chemical proteomics to find NR0B1 as a druggable dependency in KEAP1-mutant lung cancer (Cell 2017).

edges.period: 2010s (Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Fulbright fellow)
edges.work: Found that lysosomal mTORC2-PHLPP1-Akt signalling regulates chaperone-mediated autophagy (Mol Cell 2015).
edges.own_lab: Arias Lab, Albert Einstein College of Medicine (Bronx, New York, USA)
edges.focus: Chaperone-mediated autophagy and proteostasis in metabolic disorders and in the progression from liver damage to liver cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies a very selective cell-cleaning system and how its failure with age helps liver disease turn into cancer.

edges.work: Generated dynamin 1 knockout mice and showed an activity-dependent need for dynamin 1 in synaptic vesicle recycling (Science 2007).
edges.own_lab: Ferguson Lab, Yale School of Medicine (New Haven, Connecticut, USA)
edges.focus: Lysosome biology and nutrient signalling (FLCN/FNIP, TFE3/TFEB) in neurons, microglia and macrophages, and its role in neurodegeneration.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies the cell's recycling centres (lysosomes) in brain and immune cells, and how their failure leads to diseases like Parkinson's and ALS.

edges.work: PhD in membrane traffic and phosphoinositide biology at Yale before the Sabatini postdoc.
edges.own_lab: Zoncu Lab, Dept. of Molecular and Cell Biology, University of California, Berkeley (Berkeley, California, USA)

edges.period: PhD 2017-2023, postdoc 2023-2025 (MPI for Biology of Ageing, Cologne)
edges.work: Showed that mTORC1 is split in space: a lysosomal pool and a cytoplasmic pool respond to different amino-acid sources and phosphorylate different substrates (Nat Cell Biol 2024).
edges.own_lab: Fernandes Group (Muscle Metabolism and Ageing), Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing (Cologne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany)
edges.focus: Nutrient signalling and mTORC1 in skeletal muscle metabolism and ageing.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how muscle cells sense food through mTOR, and how that changes as we age.

edges.work: Showed that the four Rag GTPase paralogues are not interchangeable: RagC/D decides which substrates mTORC1 picks, RagA/B sets the response to amino-acid withdrawal (Nat Cell Biol 2022).
Co-authored the studies on the spatial split of mTORC1 by amino-acid source and on malonyl-CoA as a direct mTORC1 inhibitor.
edges.own_lab: Nuchel Lab, Center for Biochemistry, Medical Faculty, University of Cologne (Cologne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany)
edges.focus: Metabolic regulation of mTORC1 signalling in his own junior group.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how the cell's own metabolic by-products tune the mTOR growth switch.

edges.work: Showed that protein-tyrosine phosphatases work through a cysteine-phosphate intermediate (Cys215).
edges.own_lab: Guan Lab, University of California San Diego (La Jolla, California, USA)
edges.focus: Nutrient and growth-factor control of mTORC1 (TSC2 regulation by Akt and AMPK, Rag GTPases, Arf1-dependent glutamine sensing) and Hippo-YAP signalling.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how a cell decides whether it has enough food and energy to grow, and the molecular switches that turn mTOR on or off.

edges.work: Worked on Xenopus ribosomal S6 kinase II (later RSK), including its cloning and two-kinase-domain structure.
edges.own_lab: Blenis Lab, Weill Cornell Medicine (New York, New York, USA)
edges.focus: ERK/RSK and mTOR/S6K signalling, crosstalk between Ras-MAPK and mTORC1, and cancer metabolism.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies the relay chains of enzymes that carry 'grow' signals from outside the cell to its protein factories.

edges.work: Ran genome-wide yeast lifespan screens showing that lower TOR signalling extends lifespan (Genes Dev 2006).
Showed that MAPK phosphatase 1 (MKP-1) tunes pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines in innate immunity.
edges.own_lab: Chi Lab, St. Jude Children's Research Hospital (Memphis, Tennessee, USA)
edges.focus: Immunometabolism: mTOR, nutrient and metabolic signalling controlling T cell and Treg fate, function and anti-tumour immunity.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how immune cells use nutrients and the mTOR switch to decide what kind of defender to become.

edges.work: Studies mTOR in brain blood vessels; co-discovered that harmful tau enters brain endothelial cells and drives their senescence.
edges.focus: mTOR-driven cerebrovascular dysfunction and endothelial senescence in Alzheimer's disease and tauopathy.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how the brain's tiny blood vessels get damaged in Alzheimer's disease, and the role of mTOR.

edges.work: Solved cryo-EM structures of cytokine receptor complexes, including the IL-10 receptor and full-length JAK1.
Showed that soluble antigen removes self-reactive B cells inside germinal centres (Nature 1995).
Showed that leucine activates mTORC1 through the Rags while glutamine uses a Rag-independent route that needs Arf1 and the v-ATPase (Science 2015).
edges.own_lab: Jewell Lab, Dept. of Molecular Biology, UT Southwestern Medical Center (Dallas, Texas, USA)
edges.focus: How cells sense specific nutrients to control mTORC1, growth and metabolism, and how this fails in disease including cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how a cell 'tastes' particular nutrients and uses that to decide whether to grow.

edges.work: Studied the yeast sirtuin Sir2: how its NAD-dependent activity controls silencing and replicative lifespan.
edges.focus: Genetic and drug-based slowing of aging in yeast, worms, mice and companion dogs, especially rapamycin and dietary restriction.
edges.focus_beginner: He tests which genes and drugs, such as rapamycin, can slow aging in yeast, worms, mice and even pet dogs.

edges.work: Found the sir4-42 mutation that extends yeast replicative lifespan, the first link between sirtuin-family silencing proteins and aging (Cell 1995).
edges.own_lab: Kennedy Lab, Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore (Singapore)
edges.focus: Mechanisms of aging and their translation into interventions, including TOR signalling, yeast replicative aging and human healthy-longevity biomarkers.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies why we age, from yeast cells to people, and looks for ways to keep people healthy for longer.

edges.work: Showed that mTORC2 sits at contact sites between the ER and mitochondria (MAM), where mTORC2-Akt signalling keeps these contacts and mitochondria working (PNAS 2013).
Built an mTOR-driven mouse model of fatty liver turning into liver cancer and showed that liver mTORC2 drives tumours by boosting fat, sphingolipid and cardiolipin synthesis (Cancer Cell 2017).
Started the lab's rapamycin project in yeast, which found FPR1 (FKBP) and the TOR1 and TOR2 genes (Science 1991).
edges.own_lab: Heitman Lab, Duke University School of Medicine (Durham, North Carolina, USA)
edges.focus: Fungal pathogenesis and sexual reproduction (Cryptococcus, Candida), calcineurin and TOR signalling in fungi, and how immunosuppressive and antifungal drugs act.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies fungi that make people sick and how drugs like rapamycin act on them.

edges.work: Showed that a mammalian TORC2 (mTOR, mLST8, rictor) exists, is rapamycin-insensitive and controls the actin cytoskeleton (Nat Cell Biol 2004).
edges.own_lab: Jacinto Lab, Dept. of Biochemistry & Molecular Biology, Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School (Piscataway, New Jersey, USA)
edges.focus: mTORC2 regulation and substrates (Akt, SGK, PKC), co-translational phosphorylation, and how mTORC2 links nutrient metabolism such as the hexosamine pathway to growth and cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: She helped discover the second mTOR machine (mTORC2) and studies how it helps cells survive and use nutrients.

edges.work: Co-discovered the two yeast TOR complexes, TORC1 (rapamycin-sensitive) and TORC2 (rapamycin-insensitive), by purifying TOR partners (Mol Cell 2002).
edges.own_lab: Loewith Lab, Dept. of Molecular & Cellular Biology, University of Geneva (Geneva, Switzerland)
edges.focus: Upstream regulation of yeast TORC1 and TORC2, including TORC1 inhibition by glucose starvation and TORC2 control of plasma-membrane and sphingolipid balance.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how yeast cells sense food and stress at their surface and pass that news to the TOR growth switches.

edges.work: Used proteomics to identify PRAS40 and PRR5L as new mTOR-binding proteins (PLoS One 2007).
edges.own_lab: Lab for Metabolic Signaling (Thedieck Lab), Faculty of Medicine, University of Duisburg-Essen (Essen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany)
edges.focus: Systems biology of the insulin-mTOR network: data-fitted dynamic models and the coupling of mTOR with AMPK and stress granules.
edges.focus_beginner: She builds computer models, checked against experiments, of how insulin and nutrients flip the mTOR switch over time.

edges.work: Showed that a short piece of yeast MATalpha2 is enough to send a protein into the nucleus, an early study of nuclear localization signals.
edges.own_lab: Hall Lab, Biozentrum, University of Basel (Basel, Switzerland)

edges.work: Showed that adhesion and growth-arrest signals regulate the NF2 tumour suppressor merlin.
Identified the ULK1-ATG13-FIP200 complex and showed that mTOR phosphorylates it according to nutrient supply (J Biol Chem 2009).
Showed that kynurenic acid protects against ischaemia by activating GPR35, which moves to mitochondria and stabilises ATP synthase (Science 2022).
Studied MAP kinase (JNK) signalling in T cells.
Showed that arsenite blocks NF-kB activation by binding a key cysteine in IKK.
Ran a genome-wide RNAi longevity screen in C. elegans and showed that lowering TOR and protein synthesis extends lifespan.
edges.own_lab: Hansen Lab, Buck Institute for Research on Aging (Novato, California, USA)
edges.focus: Autophagy and lysosomal mechanisms in lifespan extension, especially downstream of TOR inhibition and dietary restriction in C. elegans.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how the cell's recycling system (autophagy) helps worms live longer, and what that means for human aging.

edges.work: Showed that cells from longer-lived mammal species resist oxidative and other stresses better.
Showed that oncogenic APC mutations switch on mTORC1 through GSK-3 in mice and zebrafish (2013).
Studies how the circadian clock and feeding time shape mTOR signalling and metabolism in mice.
Showed in mice that halving MLL3 gene dosage drives acute myeloid leukaemia (Cancer Cell 2014).
PhD on new programmed cell-death pathways in yeast; contributed to the spermidine and autophagy longevity work.
edges.own_lab: AG Buttner, Institute of Integrative Cell Biology and Physiology, University of Munster (Munster, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany)
edges.focus: Yeast and fly models of neurodegeneration (alpha-synuclein, Parkinson's disease), cell death and autophagy.
edges.focus_beginner: She uses yeast and fruit flies to understand why brain cells die in diseases like Parkinson's.

edges.work: Showed that mTORC1 drives pyrimidine synthesis through S6K1 phosphorylation of CAD, and purine synthesis through ATF4-MTHFD2.
edges.own_lab: Ben-Sahra Lab, Dept. of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (Chicago, Illinois, USA)
edges.focus: Signalling control of nucleotide and one-carbon/SAM metabolism by mTORC1 and MAPK/ERK in cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how growth signals tell cells to make more DNA and RNA building blocks, and how tumours exploit this.

edges.work: Identified TBC1D7 as the third core subunit of the TSC complex and studied mTORC2 regulation.
edges.own_lab: Dibble Lab, Dept. of Pathology, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center / Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: PI3K signalling control of metabolism, especially a regulatory link between PI3K and coenzyme A synthesis.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how growth signals control the cell's supply of coenzyme A, a molecule almost every metabolic reaction needs.

edges.work: Found links between PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 signalling and nucleotide and NADP/redox metabolism.
edges.own_lab: Hoxhaj Lab, Children's Medical Center Research Institute at UT Southwestern (Dallas, Texas, USA)
edges.focus: Signalling control of NAD(P) and redox metabolism in cancer and physiology.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how growth signals manage the cell's 'charged batteries' (NAD and NADPH) that power building and defence.

edges.work: Thesis on liver mTORC1: showed that dietary protein, not insulin, is the main driver of liver mTORC1 after a meal.
edges.focus: Physiological hierarchy of insulin, dietary protein and glucagon in liver and muscle mTORC1 regulation.
edges.focus_beginner: She tested in mice what actually switches on mTOR in the liver after eating, and found that protein in the meal matters most.

edges.work: Showed that insulin, through Akt phosphorylation of TSC2, makes the TSC complex leave the lysosome so Rheb can switch on mTORC1 (Cell 2014).
edges.focus: Spatial control of the TSC complex and mTORC1 at the lysosome; later drug-discovery biology.
edges.focus_beginner: She showed that insulin works partly by moving the mTOR 'brake' (TSC) away from where mTOR sits.

edges.work: Found nucleotide-synthesis dependencies of TSC-deficient, mTORC1-driven tumour cells that can be targeted.
edges.own_lab: Valvezan Lab, Center for Advanced Biotechnology and Medicine, Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School (Piscataway, New Jersey, USA)
edges.focus: How oncogenic signalling coordinates metabolic networks for growth, and how to exploit mTORC1-driven tumour dependencies such as purine synthesis.
edges.focus_beginner: He looks for metabolic weak spots in tumours where mTOR is stuck 'on', so drugs can hit cancer cells and spare normal ones.

edges.work: Showed that irreversible inactivation of APC/C-Cdh1 is the point of no return for entering the cell cycle (Cell 2016).
edges.own_lab: Cappell Lab, Laboratory of Cancer Biology and Genetics, National Cancer Institute (Bethesda, Maryland, USA)
edges.focus: Live single-cell imaging of cell-cycle entry, including how mTOR briefly switches off APC/C to give cells a pulse of glycolysis.
edges.focus_beginner: He films single living cells to see the exact moment they decide to divide, and how mTOR helps fuel that step.

edges.work: Worked out the parts of the mitochondrial calcium uniporter, including EMRE.
First author of a 2026 Nature study on a TBK1/ULK1-FNIP1 axis that couples lysosomal stress to TFEB activation.
edges.focus: Lysosomal stress signalling, FLCN-FNIP regulation and substrate-specific mTORC1-TFEB control.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how a stressed lysosome raises an alarm that switches on the cell's cleanup program.

edges.work: Showed that TOR blocks autophagy by keeping Atg13 heavily phosphorylated, which stops the Atg1 kinase complex from forming (J Cell Biol 2000).
edges.own_lab: Kamada Group, National Institute for Basic Biology (Okazaki, Japan)
edges.focus: Yeast TORC1: amino-acid sensing (free tRNA as a starvation signal), Atg13 phosphorylation and translation control.
edges.focus_beginner: He showed how the TOR switch stops yeast cells from recycling themselves when food is plentiful.

edges.work: Discovered the Atg12-Atg5 conjugation system that autophagy needs (Nature 1998), the first ubiquitin-like system found in autophagy.
edges.own_lab: Mizushima Laboratory, Graduate School of Medicine, University of Tokyo (Tokyo, Japan)
edges.focus: Mechanisms and physiology of autophagy in mammals, from autophagosome formation to its roles in development and disease.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how mammal cells build the 'rubbish bags' that carry worn-out parts to be recycled.

edges.period: PhD until 1991 (Johns Hopkins), postdoc MIT until 1993
edges.work: Solved the crystal structure of the Zif268 zinc finger bound to DNA (Science 1991).
Solved crystal and cryo-EM structures of mTOR-mLST8 and mTORC1, showing how Rheb switches the kinase on and how PRAS40 and rapamycin-FKBP12 block substrates.
edges.focus: Structural mechanisms of mTOR kinase regulation, substrate recruitment (TOS motif, FRB site) and cancer-associated activating mutations.
edges.focus_beginner: She makes atom-level 3D pictures of the mTOR machine to see how it is switched on and how drugs jam it.

edges.work: PhD on translational control downstream of mTOR (4E-BP1 and eIF4E).
edges.own_lab: Tee Lab, Division of Cancer & Genetics, Cardiff University (Cardiff, Wales, UK)

edges.work: Showed that where lysosomes sit in the cell, set by internal pH, coordinates mTORC1 signalling with autophagosome formation (Nat Cell Biol 2011).
edges.own_lab: Korolchuk Lab, Newcastle University (Newcastle upon Tyne, UK)
edges.focus: Nutrient sensing by mTORC1 (including pH), selective autophagy adaptors such as p62, and autophagy in the DNA damage response, senescence and aging.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how cells sense nutrients and decide when to recycle their own parts, and how this changes as we age.

edges.work: Used ribosome profiling to map how oncogenic mTOR changes translation in prostate cancer, and showed that the mTOR inhibitor INK128 blocks pro-invasion mRNA translation and metastasis (Nature 2012).
edges.own_lab: Hsieh Lab, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center (Seattle, Washington, USA)
edges.focus: How deregulated protein synthesis shapes cell fate, tumour initiation, progression and drug resistance in prostate and bladder cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how prostate and bladder cancers change the way cells make proteins, and how that helps tumours resist treatment.

edges.work: Showed how lineage regulators switch on the C. elegans gene unc-86 in one daughter of each dividing neuroblast.
edges.own_lab: Baumeister Lab, Bioinformatics and Molecular Genetics, Institute of Biology III, University of Freiburg (Freiburg, Germany)
edges.focus: C. elegans genetics of ageing and neurodegeneration; hosted the Thedieck group that built the dynamic insulin-mTOR model.
edges.focus_beginner: He uses tiny worms to find genes that control ageing and brain-cell health.

edges.work: Showed that dopamine and glutamate regulate striatal acetylcholine release during decision-making (Nature 2023).
Developed LysoIP for fast lysosome isolation and lysosomal metabolomics, showing v-ATPase and mTOR-dependent control of amino-acid efflux.
edges.own_lab: Abu-Remaileh Lab, Depts. of Chemical Engineering and Genetics, Sarafan ChEM-H, Stanford University (Stanford, California, USA)
edges.focus: Lysosomal metabolism and lipid biochemistry (BMP, CLN5, PLA2G15) and how lysosome failure drives neurodegeneration, cancer and metabolic disease.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies what is inside the cell's recycling bins (lysosomes), and how jammed recycling leads to brain diseases.

edges.work: Identified Ragulator as the GEF that switches the Rags on, and GATOR1 as the GAP that switches them off, a tumour-suppressor complex mutated in cancer.
edges.own_lab: Bar-Peled Lab, Center for Cancer Research, Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: Chemical proteomics of reactive cysteines to find druggable cancer dependencies; NRF2/KEAP1 and redox stress signalling in lung cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He uses chemistry to find weak spots on cancer-cell proteins where new drugs could attach.

edges.work: Found that the Sestrins act through GATOR2 and identified CASTOR1 as the cytosolic arginine sensor for mTORC1.
edges.own_lab: Chantranupong Lab, Dept. of Biology, Boston University (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: How neurons rewire core metabolic and signalling pathways, including mTOR, for cell-type-specific needs, and why some neurons are selectively vulnerable in neurodegeneration.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies the special 'diets' of different brain cells, and why some brain cells die in diseases like Parkinson's while others survive.

edges.work: Ran genome-wide CRISPR screens cataloguing mTORC1 regulators and showed that AMPK and HRI-ATF4 relay mitochondrial dysfunction to mTORC1.
Made RagA-GTP knock-in mice and showed that Rag-dependent mTORC1 control is essential for autophagy and survival right after birth.
edges.own_lab: Metabolism and Cell Signalling Group, Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) (Madrid, Spain)
edges.focus: Whole-body physiology of nutrient sensing by mTORC1 and the Rag GTPases: B-cell activation and germinal centres, follicular lymphoma, and the mTOR-autophagy axis in obesity.
edges.focus_beginner: He uses mice to see what happens to the whole body, including immune cells and cancers, when the cell's nutrient sensor is broken or stuck on.

edges.work: First author on mTOR resistance-mutation work (2014) and co-author on the GATOR and Sestrin papers.
Used rictor and mLST8 knockout mice to define what mTORC2 does in the whole animal (Akt-FOXO and PKC-alpha signalling).
edges.own_lab: Guertin Lab, Program in Molecular Medicine, UMass Chan Medical School (Worcester, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: mTORC2 and nutrient sensing in adipose tissue and liver: brown fat development and thermogenesis, lipid metabolism, obesity, diabetes and cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how fat tissue, especially 'brown fat' that burns energy to make heat, uses mTOR signals to manage the body's energy.

edges.work: Mapped the mTOR-regulated phosphoproteome and identified Grb10 as an mTORC1 substrate that feeds back to inhibit PI3K.
edges.focus: How nutrient conditions change cancer-cell sensitivity to metabolic drugs, with a focus on lung cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: She is a lung-cancer doctor and scientist who studies how a tumour's food supply changes which drugs work.

edges.work: Showed that tumours with constantly active PI3K do not respond to dietary restriction.
edges.own_lab: Kalaany Lab, Division of Endocrinology, Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: How whole-body metabolism (insulin/IGF signalling, diet, obesity) shapes cancer incidence and growth, and tumour metabolic dependencies in lung and pancreatic cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how what the whole body eats and stores, including blood sugar and insulin, makes tumours grow faster or slower.

edges.work: Showed that rapamycin causes insulin resistance by disrupting mTORC2, while lowering mTORC1 alone can extend lifespan without hurting glucose control.
edges.own_lab: Lamming Lab, Division of Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, University of Wisconsin-Madison (Madison, Wisconsin, USA)
edges.focus: Dietary protein and branched-chain amino acids as regulators of metabolic health and longevity through mTOR, mTORC2 biology, and safer geroprotective rapamycin regimens.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how the amount and kind of protein we eat, acting through mTOR, affects weight, diabetes and how long mice live.

edges.work: Showed that mTORC1 switches on SREBP-1c and fat production in the liver, and worked on DEPTOR.
edges.own_lab: Laplante Lab, CRIUCPQ, Universite Laval (Quebec City, Quebec, Canada)
edges.focus: DEPTOR and mTOR signalling in fat-cell formation, obesity and liver metabolism.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how mTOR and its brake protein DEPTOR control the making of fat cells and fat in the liver.

edges.work: Discovered DEPTOR, a natural brake on mTOR that is overexpressed in some multiple myelomas, and worked on where mTORC1 sits in the cell.
edges.focus: Genetics-based mapping of how drugs such as rapamycin and metformin act, and the genetic and environmental bases of aging.
edges.focus_beginner: He tries to work out exactly how common drugs like rapamycin act inside cells, and what that means for aging.

edges.work: Solved the 3.2 A cryo-EM structure of raptor bound to Rag-Ragulator, showing how mTORC1 docks on the lysosome.
edges.own_lab: Rogala Lab, Depts. of Structural Biology and Chemical & Systems Biology, Stanford University School of Medicine (Stanford, California, USA)
edges.focus: Structural and chemical biology of nutrient sensors and transporters and their integration with hormone signals; chemical probes for growth pathways in cancer and TSC.
edges.focus_beginner: He builds atom-level 3D models of the proteins that sense food inside cells, and designs chemicals that turn them up or down.

edges.work: Showed that the Rag GTPases bind raptor and carry the amino-acid signal to mTORC1, that Ragulator anchors them on the lysosome, and identified PRAS40 as an mTORC1 substrate.
edges.own_lab: Sancak Lab, Dept. of Pharmacology, University of Washington (Seattle, Washington, USA)
edges.focus: Mitochondrial calcium uptake through the uniporter (MCU complex) and how it regulates mitochondrial metabolism, innate immunity and cell death.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies how calcium gets into mitochondria, the cell's power plants, and how that turns their energy output up or down.

edges.work: Co-discovered rictor and mTORC2, showed that mTORC2 phosphorylates Akt at Ser473, and that prolonged rapamycin blocks mTORC2 assembly.
edges.own_lab: Sarbassov Group, School of Sciences and Humanities, Nazarbayev University (Astana, Kazakhstan)
edges.focus: Growth-factor and nutrient-dependent mTOR signalling, ribosome biogenesis, and how this signalling goes wrong in cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how mTOR and the 'survival' protein Akt get stuck on in cancer cells, and how that could be blocked.

edges.period: PhD 2018 (MIT Biology; co-advised with Thomas U. Schwartz)
edges.work: Solved the crystal structures of Sestrin2 with leucine and CASTOR1 with arginine, showing how amino acids are recognized upstream of mTORC1.
edges.own_lab: Saxton Lab, Dept. of Molecular and Cell Biology, University of California, Berkeley (Berkeley, California, USA)
edges.focus: Structure-guided engineering of cytokines and receptors to reprogram immune-cell communication for autoimmunity, cancer and infection.
edges.focus_beginner: He redesigns the chemical 'messages' immune cells send each other so they can work as better medicines.

edges.work: Showed that liver mTORC1 controls ketone-body production during fasting through PPAR-alpha, and that this control changes with age.
Characterized Torin1, an ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor that revealed functions of mTORC1 rapamycin cannot block, and later a model of how mTORC1 controls TOP-mRNA translation.
edges.own_lab: Thoreen Lab, Dept. of Cellular & Molecular Physiology, Yale School of Medicine (New Haven, Connecticut, USA)
edges.focus: How 5'TOP motifs, LARP1 and eIF4F set how strongly an mRNA depends on mTOR, and how that control is used in physiology.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how mTOR decides which protein 'recipes' (mRNAs) the cell's protein factories read first when food is plentiful.

edges.period: about 2010-2017 (PhD 2017, MIT Biology; co-advised with Eric S. Lander)
edges.work: Developed genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screens in human cells and defined the genes human cells cannot live without.
edges.focus: Moved to systems neuroscience: structural and functional organization of neocortical circuits.
edges.focus_beginner: After inventing a way to switch off every gene one by one, he moved on to studying how brain circuits are wired.

edges.period: PhD 2017 (MIT Biology); MD Harvard Medical School
edges.work: Showed that Sestrin2 is a direct leucine sensor for mTORC1, binding leucine at about the concentration that half-activates the pathway.
edges.own_lab: Wolfson Lab, Dept. of Cell Biology, Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: Interoception: how visceral sensory neurons detect signals from internal organs such as the gut, and how they shape physiology and disease.
edges.focus_beginner: She studies the nerves that let your brain 'feel' what is going on inside your body, such as a full or upset stomach.

edges.work: Showed that SLC38A9 senses arginine and also exports essential amino acids such as leucine from lysosomes; co-developed rapid lysosome purification (LysoIP).
edges.own_lab: Wyant Lab, Cardiovascular Research Center, Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: How oxygen, nutrients, stretch and electrical activity regulate heart and skeletal muscle, aiming at muscle atrophy, heart failure and cachexia.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how heart and muscle cells sense oxygen, food and exercise, to find ways to stop muscle wasting and heart failure.

edges.work: Showed that mTORC1 senses amino acids 'inside-out', starting in the lysosome lumen and requiring the v-ATPase.
edges.own_lab: Zoncu Lab, Dept. of Molecular and Cell Biology, University of California, Berkeley (Berkeley, California, USA)
edges.focus: The lysosome as a signalling hub: cholesterol sensing via SLC38A9/NPC1 and OSBP, FLCN-RagC control of TFEB, and lysosomal quality control in disease.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies the lysosome, the cell's recycling centre, as a 'control tower' that tells mTOR whether nutrients such as cholesterol are available.

edges.work: Showed that S6K1 phosphorylates the clock protein BMAL1, linking mTOR to daily rhythms of protein synthesis, and that constant mTOR activity in tuberous sclerosis models disturbs the clock.
edges.own_lab: Lipton Lab, F.M. Kirby Neurobiology Center, Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard Medical School (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: How mTOR and the circadian clock interact in the brain, with a focus on sleep and neurodevelopmental disorders.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies how the mTOR switch and the body clock talk to each other, and why this matters for sleep in children with brain disorders.

edges.work: Worked on catalytic antibodies.
Showed that long-term IGF-I exposure reduces autophagy and viability in human fibroblasts, and studied rapamycin in senescent cells.
Studied how p53 suppresses tumours, separating its DNA-damage response from its oncogene response through ARF.
Purified the mRNA cap-binding protein, later named eIF4E, the protein through which mTOR controls translation (PNAS 1979).
Showed that AMPK directly phosphorylates ULK1/ULK2, linking energy sensing to autophagy and mitophagy (Science 2011), and developed ULK1 inhibitors.
edges.focus: AMPK-ULK1 signalling in autophagy; ULK1 substrates and inhibitors.
edges.focus_beginner: He found the direct link by which the cell's fuel gauge switches on its recycling system.

edges.work: Engineered protein kinases with changed nucleotide and inhibitor specificity, the chemical-genetics approach of the Shokat lab.
edges.focus: Drug discovery of kinase inhibitors, including ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitors.
edges.focus_beginner: He turned lab chemistry into companies that make drugs blocking mTOR and other cancer enzymes.

edges.work: Used lacZ gene fusions in E. coli to study how outer membrane proteins such as LamB are exported and placed in the membrane.
edges.own_lab: Hall Lab, Biozentrum, University of Basel (Basel, Switzerland)
edges.focus: Discovered TOR1/TOR2 in yeast and defined TORC1 and TORC2; later mTOR in mammalian growth, metabolism and cancer.
edges.focus_beginner: He found the main 'grow or don't grow' switch in cells (TOR) and showed that it works as two separate machines.

edges.work: Showed in yeast that the Sir2 relative Hst2 drives Sir2-independent lifespan extension by calorie restriction (Science 2005).
Purified RAFT1 (mTOR), the mammalian protein that binds FKBP12 only in the presence of rapamycin, and showed that it phosphorylates S6K and 4E-BP1.
edges.own_lab: Sabatini group, Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry of the Czech Academy of Sciences (Prague, Czech Republic), with a branch in Boston (Boston, Massachusetts, USA)
edges.focus: Built out the mTORC1 and mTORC2 pathway: raptor, rictor, the Rag GTPases, Ragulator, GATOR1/2, Sestrin2 as a leucine sensor, CASTOR1 as an arginine sensor, SLC38A9 and lysosomal metabolomics.
edges.focus_beginner: He found the parts that let a cell 'taste' how many amino acids it has and pass that message to mTOR, the master switch that decides whether the cell builds or saves.

edges.work: Studied the structural and functional organisation of neocortical circuits.
Showed that when amino acids or growth factors run out, the Rag GTPases pull TSC2 to the lysosome, where it switches off Rheb and releases mTORC1 (Cell 2014).
edges.own_lab: Demetriades Group, Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing (Cologne, Germany)
edges.focus: Spatial regulation of mTORC1 by amino acids and stress (TSC2, Rags, lysosomal and non-lysosomal mTORC1 pools) and its relevance to ageing.
edges.focus_beginner: He studies where in the cell the mTOR switch is turned off when food runs out, and what that means for ageing.

edges.work: Studied how Munc18c and syntaxin 4 control insulin secretion and glucose uptake.
Linked the ribonuclease activity of angiogenin to its ability to grow blood vessels.
Studies innate antiviral immunity, including how SP140 controls interferon-beta mRNA stability.
Studied how nutrient conditions change cancer-cell sensitivity to metabolic drugs.
Found a 'switch-helix' in eIF2B that coordinates control of the integrated stress response (Nat Chem Biol 2023).
PhD in enzyme biochemistry (aldehyde dehydrogenase) at Purdue.
edges.own_lab: Guan Lab, University of California San Diego (La Jolla, California, USA)

edges.work: First author of the Kobe raptor paper (Cell 2002), published side by side with the Sabatini lab, showing raptor is the mTOR scaffold needed for 4E-BP1 and S6K phosphorylation.
Studied how the Rag GTPases regulate mTORC1, including the cryo-EM structure of the lysosomal FLCN-FNIP2-Rag-Ragulator complex.
edges.own_lab: Lawrence Lab, Dept. of Biological Chemistry, UCLA (Los Angeles, California, USA)
edges.focus: Own lab at UCLA; focus building on lysosomal mTORC1 signalling and the integrated stress response.
edges.focus_beginner: She now runs her own lab studying how cells sense stress and nutrients and decide when to pause growth.
